segments.narration: A wooden machine beat Napoleon at chess in 1809. Schonbrunn Palace, Vienna: a life-size figure in robes, bolted to a cabinet of gears.
Wolfgang von Kempelen built it in 1770 for Empress Maria Theresa. Before each game he opened the cabinet doors to prove nothing was inside.
It played Benjamin Franklin. It toured London, Leipzig, Havana, Baltimore. Eighty-four years on the road, mostly winning.
So how does a box of cogs read a chessboard? Edgar Allan Poe published his theory in 1836 and got most of it wrong.
A man was folded inside on a sliding seat, reading moves off magnets under each square. In 1827 the operator fainted in Baltimore and two boys watched him climb out.

verdicts.claim: In 1809 Napoleon Bonaparte played the Mechanical Turk at Schonbrunn Palace and lost, resigning after 19 moves.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia: lost to Napoleon at Schonbrunn in 1809, Napoleon resigned after 19 moves. Narration says only that the machine beat him.

verdicts.claim: A human operator sat concealed in the cabinet on a sliding seat, reading moves from magnets under the board's squares; in 1827 operator William Schlumberger fainted in Baltimore and two boys saw him climb out.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia describes the sliding seat, the magnets under the 64 squares and the 1827 Baltimore fainting seen by two boys, reported in the Baltimore Gazette on 1 June 1827.
